AgentSetupResponse.description:
Org-level agent setup for the drawer: the org's `o2syn_` token plus the
ingredients the UI composes per-platform install commands from (the
location name is typed client-side, so the server returns parts, not a
finished command). Private locations are deploy-declared (`AGENT_LOCATION`),
so setup is org-level — the location row is upserted at first register.

install.description:
Legacy docker one-liner (kept while the drawer migrates to composed
per-platform commands).

org.description: Org the probe scopes its Job API calls to (`AGENT_ORG`, in the URL path).

script_url.description: Public install script the composed commands pipe to bash.

AgentTokenSecret.description:
A freshly created/rotated token — the ONLY response that carries the raw
value (shown once, then only ever masked).

having.description:
CRITICAL threshold. `having.value` is untyped (`serde_json::Value`) and
may be an int, a float, or a numeric string.

multi_alert.description:
Opt-in to per-group evaluation — multi-alerts, `alerts_2.md` M-9/D26.

`#[serde(default)]` is the whole backward-compatibility guarantee: an
aggregation stored before this field existed cannot contain it, so it
deserializes to `false` and the alert keeps its legacy collapsed
evaluation byte-for-byte. Nothing is inferred from `group_by` being
present — that would silently change paging cadence and reset silence
fingerprints for every existing grouped alert.

Validated by [`grouping::validate_multi_alert`] (M-10): requires a
non-empty `group_by`, an orderable `having.operator`, and "any group"
count gates.

warning_value.description:
WARNING threshold, sharing `having.operator` and `having.column` with
critical (alerts_2.md §4.4). `None` = single-level aggregation alert,
i.e. exactly the legacy behaviour. Stored as f64 because aggregate
values (averages, percentiles) are not integers.
Same lenient deserialization as `promql_warning_value`, for the same
reason (D61) — aggregate warnings are the field most likely to be
fractional.

AiCreditCosts.description: Credits per AI feature: the configured cost of one operation, or the credits it used.

AiUsageResponse.description: AI usage response for the API

payer_org_id.description: Set for a billing-group member, whose payer org holds the subscription.

oneOf.description: Free credits each feature used; `None` when the breakdown could not be read.

creates_incident.description:
When true, this alert creates/joins incidents instead of sending direct notifications.
Notification is sent only when a new incident is created or a new alert type joins
an existing incident. Repeated firings are suppressed.
When false (default), the alert sends notifications directly and does not correlate
to any incident.

keep_firing_for.description:
Seconds the condition must stay clear before the episode recovers.
0 recovers on the first clear evaluation, which is what every alert does
today. Named after Prometheus' `keep_firing_for`, with the same meaning.

notify_on_recovery.description:

silence, or delivery (PT-5 / D19). B-29 carved out one exception:
when set, it takes precedence over the eval_level default for
incident severity at creation/escalation — see
`config::meta::alerts::priority` and
`core::alerts::incidents::create_new_incident`.

integer via serde `try_from`/`into`; without it the generated OpenAPI

one moment nobody has the patience to debug a URL.

notification payloads with no validation. These are the filtering /
scoping primitive.

Skipped when empty so alerts that set no tags serialize exactly as
they did before Feature 2 (G5).

CountSource.description:
How a count SLI obtains good/total — itself a tagged union so that
unrepresentable states cannot be constructed (D40).
**Adjacently tagged, not internally tagged.** This workspace builds
`serde_json` with `arbitrary_precision` (root `Cargo.toml`), which encodes
every number as a map. Internally-tagged enums buffer their whole subtree
through `serde::__private::de::Content` before dispatching, and that
buffered map cannot then be deserialized into an `f64` — the failure is
`invalid type: map, expected f64`, and it survives nesting. Serialization
still succeeds, so the bug only appears on read-back.

This variant carries no numbers *today*, but the dual-query form is the one
most likely to gain them, and the failure mode is silent enough to be worth
pre-empting. See [`SliConfig`] for the same treatment and a regression test.

The native form: one scan, so good and total are provably from the same

Importer-only fallback for an unfoldable imported pair. Weaker
atomicity: two scans that cannot be proven to have seen the same

query.description:
Importer-only fallback for an unfoldable imported pair. Weaker

oneOf.description:
Metrics-native counting: two PromQL expressions, each evaluated per
slice (wire tag `prom_ql`, following [`QueryLanguage::PromQl`]).

Exists because pre-aggregated counters have no rows for a `good_expr`
to classify — "good" only exists as arithmetic between series, and
correct counter arithmetic is `increase()` (monotonic-reset-aware),
which SQL over raw samples cannot express. The expressions should use
a range selector equal to the slice interval
(`increase(http_requests_total[5m])` for a 5-minute slice); the
evaluator samples them at slice ends, so each sample covers exactly
its slice.

Same atomicity caveat as [`Self::DualQuery`]: two evaluations that
cannot be proven to have seen the same instant. Grouping needs no
column list — the returned series' labels supply the group values.

query.description:
Metrics-native counting: two PromQL expressions, each evaluated per
slice (wire tag `prom_ql`, following [`QueryLanguage::PromQl`]).

Exists because pre-aggregated counters have no rows for a `good_expr`
to classify — "good" only exists as arithmetic between series, and
correct counter arithmetic is `increase()` (monotonic-reset-aware),
which SQL over raw samples cannot express. The expressions should use
a range selector equal to the slice interval
(`increase(http_requests_total[5m])` for a 5-minute slice); the
evaluator samples them at slice ends, so each sample covers exactly
its slice.

Same atomicity caveat as [`Self::DualQuery`]: two evaluations that
cannot be proven to have seen the same instant. Grouping needs no
column list — the returned series' labels supply the group values.

group.

oncall_team.description:
On-call team (a team id) this alert pages, taking precedence over
ownership discovery. Omitted or `null` means "work the owner out from the
identity dimensions", which is the normal case.

that names nothing routes nowhere, and a page that routes nowhere is

Priority 1..=5 (P1 = most urgent), Feature 2 / PT-1.

Where the fix for this alert is written down.

Copied onto every on-call response record the alert opens, so whoever is
woken is handed the link in the page instead of going to find it while
the thing is on fire.

Validated at save: `http://` or `https://` with a host, or the save is
refused. A malformed link stored today is a dead click at 3am, and the
moment it is read is the worst possible moment to discover it.

Full replace, like `oncall_team`.

Composite-only boolean condition over stable child alert IDs.

Deprecated. The destination folder is taken from the `folder` query
parameter, which is what the permission check authorizes; the default
folder is used when it is absent. A value here that disagrees with the

CreateAlertRequestBody.description:
HTTP request body for `CreateAlert` endpoint.

Creates a new alert with the specified configuration. The alert monitors
a stream (logs, metrics, or traces) and triggers notifications when conditions are met.

## Example

```json
{
    "name": "High Error Rate Alert",
    "stream_type": "logs",
    "stream_name": "default",
    "is_real_time": false,
    "query_condition": {
        "type": "sql",
        "sql": "SELECT count(*) as count FROM \"default\" WHERE level = 'error'"
    },
    "trigger_condition": {
        "period": 15,
        "operator": ">=",
        "threshold": 100,
        "frequency": 5,
        "frequency_type": "minutes",
        "silence": 60
    },
    "destinations": ["slack-alerts"],
    "enabled": true,
    "description": "Alert when error count exceeds 100 in 15 minutes"
}
```

alert_budget_per_day.description: Delivered-alert budget per day; mutually exclusive with `percentile` in one request.

alert_window_buckets.description: Window-share length in buckets, at least 1 and at most 24h of buckets; absent means 1.

alert_window_fire_pct.description: Percent of the window out of band that fires; absent means 100.

alert_window_recover_pct.description: Percent of the window out of band below which it recovers; absent means the fire percent.

band_width.description: Manual band half-width k in sigmas, 1 to 10; absent uses the trained k (3 to 6).

detection_window_seconds.description: At most 100,000 histogram buckets; a stored row over the limit runs clamped to it.

level_half_width_seconds.description: Accepted and stored, but ignored by the band model.

percentile.description: Legacy, read back as `threshold` for read-modify-write; k trains at p99, within 3 to 6.

priority.description:
Triage priority P1..P5 (Feature 2, PT-1). Anomaly configs appear in the
same alert list as scheduled/realtime alerts, so they carry the same
metadata. Absent = unset.

schedule_interval.description: At least 1 minute; a stored row below it runs every minute.

stream_name.description:
The stream the detector reads. Required in filters mode. In custom_sql mode it can be
left blank when the SQL reads exactly one stream, which then names it.

tags.description:
Selection tags (PT-6), normalized and validated on save exactly as for
alerts — one `normalize_tags` serves both.

template.description: Template override for this config's messages; absent, null or "" uses the destination's.

training_window_days.description: At most 3,000,000 histogram buckets; a stored row over the limit trains clamped to it.

CreateDomainResponse.description:
The DNS TXT record the admin needs to create — `txt_name`/`txt_value`

self-explanatory to a non-engineer reading it off an API response.

Where notifications go when this source's alerts create or join an

pool.description:

rotation_id.description: Omitted means the primary; an unknown rotation is refused, or a cover staffs nothing.

Alert destination configuration for sending notifications when alerts trigger.

IMPORTANT: The `template` field is REQUIRED to create an alert destination.
Without a template, the destination becomes a pipeline destination and cannot be used with
alerts.

# Example - Creating an HTTP alert destination
```json
{
  "name": "my_alert_webhook",
  "url": "https://example.com/webhook",
  "method": "post",
  "type": "http",
  "template": "Default",
  "skip_tls_verify": false
}
```

# Example - Creating an Email alert destination
```json
{
  "name": "my_email_dest",
  "type": "email",
  "emails": ["alerts@example.com", "team@example.com"],
  "template": "Default"
}
```

Request body for creating an enrichment table from a public URL.

The URL must point to a publicly accessible CSV file. Authentication-required
URLs (e.g., S3 presigned URLs with complex headers) are not currently supported.

The `append` behavior is controlled via query parameter, matching the file upload endpoint.

replace_failed.description:
Replace only the failed job's URL (optional, default: false)

When true, only updates the failed job with the new URL while keeping
all successful jobs unchanged. Useful for fixing typos or broken URLs
without re-downloading working data sources.

Public URL to the CSV file.

Requirements:
- Must start with http:// or https://
- Must be publicly accessible (no authentication)
- Should return CSV content-type (not enforced but recommended)
- File can be any size - streaming handles large files efficiently

EscalateRequest.description: "This needs more people, now." Optional context for the timeline.

destinations.description:
Alert Destination names this team pages through when a rung includes the
Webhook channel. Reuses the destinations an org already has rather than
storing URLs twice.

l0.description:
§4's L0 block: how the AI SRE agent relates to this team's paging.
Defaulted on read, because a row written before the column existed has
to behave like a team that never opened the screen.

template.description: Template override for this team's on-call messages; `None` uses each destination's.

channels.description: The channels the policy names, restricted to what this build can send.

cross_team_moves.description:
The only ways a page ever leaves this team, stated so the screen does not
have to imply one that does not exist.

There is no team hierarchy in this product — no parent team, no sibling
team, nothing above a team to climb to. A rung's targets are the whole of
who a ladder can reach, and the one real cross-team move is a responder
pressing handoff with a `to_team_id`.

ends_with.description: What happens when the ladder runs out — the "Escalation ends" line.

l0.description:
What the AI SRE does at this priority, before or beside the ladder.

Until this response carried L0 the ladder screen could not mention the
agent at all, so a deployment running one showed a P2 ladder starting at
0m when the page is in fact held for the triage budget first. The policy
stored `l0` and the engine honoured it; the read the screen is built from
omitted it.

pages_anyone.description: This priority pages a human at all.

reaches_nobody.description: Nobody at all would be reached, at any rung. A dry run's headline.

EscalationProgress.description:
Where the ladder has got to, and what happens next. The question a responder
actually has mid-incident is "when does this wake somebody else", and it was
answerable nowhere in the product.

exhausted.description: The ladder ran out of rungs with nobody acknowledging.

held_until_micros.description: While the first page is held for AI triage, the deadline the held trigger wakes at.

next_recipients.description:
Who that rung would wake, resolved against the rotations as they stand
now. Unlike `FiredRung::reached` this IS a live answer, because the
question is about a page that has not happened yet.

next_targets.description: The next rung, if the ladder is still climbing.

stopped_because.description:
Why the ladder is not climbing — acknowledged, snoozed, resolved.
`None` means it is running.

EscalationTarget.description:
One thing a level pages. A level may hold several, and they fire together.

Firing together is the only mechanism for paging more than one person. No
stacking, no overlap, no derivation — which keeps "who does this level wake"
answerable by reading it.

oneOf.description:
A named rotation, by id rather than by name: a rotation is renameable,
and a stored policy must not start paging a different position because
somebody fixed a typo on a calendar.
One named person, by email; a ladder step skips them while away, a handoff does not.

Every member of the team — the last resort at the bottom of a ladder.

Blind to rotations, and skips the away only while someone else is left: it
is where a page falls back when every rotation has failed to produce
anybody, and a last resort that filters itself down to nobody is not one.

requires `confirmCostEstimate`.

datasetName.description:
Resolved from the Dataset the experiment pinned, so callers do not have
to fetch the Dataset list just to label a run. None when it was deleted.

datasetVersion.description: The pinned `global_version`: the row cut every Slot reads.

datasetWriteVersion.description: The Dataset version to display for that pin: one per write request.

isBaseline.description:
The organization's Baseline for this Dataset. At most one Experiment per
organization and Dataset carries it.

ExperimentResultRowBody.description: One pinned Dataset case with every trial reduced to list-surface aggregates.

errorMessage.description: Sample message of the row's largest failure cause (grouped by kind, else by first line).

output.description: Present only for a single-trial row; multi-trial outputs belong in drill-down.

rowIndex.description: Zero-based position in deterministic pinned-snapshot row order.

clientScores.description:
Scores the customer's own code reported for this Slot. `scores` above is
one entry per pinned Scorer, which a client Score is not.

status.description: The one field a list surface needs; task and score statuses remain for drill-down.

clientScoreSummaries.description:
Dimensions the customer's own code reported. Empty for a run whose
Scores all came from platform Scorers.

rowDispersions.description:
Trial dispersion for the cases on this page, always measured over the
Experiment's full evidence so paging never splits a case's trials.

clientScoreSummaries.description:
Per-case aggregate of the dimensions the customer's own code reported,
kept separate from Scorer summaries because the two are not comparable.

dispersion.description:
Per-dimension trial dispersion for this case. Empty for a single-trial
Experiment, which has no disagreement to report.

outlierTrialIndex.description:
Trial the drawer opens on: the one farthest from the mean or majority in
this case's most dispersed dimension.

maxNormalized.description:
Largest normalized dispersion across this case's dimensions. This is the
key the result table flags and sorts by.

rowIndex.description: Zero-based position in deterministic pinned-snapshot row order.

ExperimentScoreOutcomesBody.description: `completed` is scored plus failed; `total` also counts pending, skipped and unscored.

name.description:
User-facing dimension label. This is the Score Config name when the
Scorer declares one, otherwise the Scorer name.

value.description: Type-aware aggregate: numeric mean, boolean counts, or categorical counts.

ExperimentSkipReason.description: Permanent evidence reason shared by Experiment execution and score records.

metadata.description:
Dataset Case metadata, so a client-side Task can branch on it without a
second read of the Dataset.

task_ref.description: Pinned `name@version` of a published Remote Task. Never latest.

task_fingerprint.description:
Immutable identity of the customer code under evaluation. Every
execution record reported for this Experiment must repeat it.

ExperimentTaskOutcomesBody.description: Slot counts over the pinned set; `pending` is `total` minus the slots that have finished.

by_secs.description: Added to the later of the current end and now.

version.description: The version the row was loaded at; a newer stored row makes the extension a 409.

created_id.description: Set when a recurring row got a one-time follow-up instead of a longer window.

ExtendDowntimeResponse.description: The row that now ends later: the extended one-time row, or the follow-up of a recurring one.

fields.description:
List of field names that are equivalent (e.g., ["host", "hostname", "node"])

Note: Field names can overlap with other groups. First-defined group wins.

group.description:
Category/group this semantic field belongs to (e.g., "Common", "Kubernetes", "AWS", "GCP",
"Azure") Used for UI organization and preset templates

is_workload_type.description:
When true, this alias is a workload-type dimension used to build identity sets.
Aliases with this flag are grouped by their `group` field to form `IdentitySet`
entries with `distinguish_by` populated from those alias IDs.
Aliases without this flag (HTTP, Database, System, etc.) are never used as
identity set discriminators.

data_type.description: Target data type (e.g., Utf8, LargeUtf8, Int64, Float64)

name.description: Field name to update

nullable.description: Optionally set nullability; defaults to existing field nullability if not provided

emptyLiteral.description:
Set when `value` is an explicit `''` from SQL, so the builder keeps `x <> ''`
instead of treating the empty value as "not entered yet".

FilterField.description: A built-in session field, or any other column of the RUM stream.

FiredRung.description: A rung that has already fired.

at.description: Absolute instant it fired, so the UI need not re-derive it.

reached.description:
The PEOPLE it actually reached, from the delivery ledger.

Read from what was recorded at the time, never re-resolved against who
holds the rotation now: a rung that woke Ana has to keep saying Ana, or a
look back at last month's page quietly rewrites who was accountable.
`targets` says why they were chosen; this says who.

reached_nobody.description:
The rung fired and the delivery ledger has nobody for it.

Distinct from an empty `reached` on a rung that is merely old: this is the
"paged nobody" case — an unstaffed rotation, or a target that resolved to
no one — and the most important thing a post-mortem learns here.

targets.description: The POSITIONS this rung names — "whoever is on call in Primary".

settings.description: The fleet's own overrides; unset fields inherit the organization defaults.

oneOf.description: Null for a fleet the caller may list but not read.

fleets.description: The readable fleets whose desired or stable version is this configuration.

fleets_hidden.description: Fleets using this configuration that the caller cannot read.

FleetSettings.description: Per-fleet overrides; `None` inherits the organization default.

offline_heartbeats.description: A collector is offline after this many missed heartbeats.

retention_days.description: Offline collectors are removed after this many days; 0 keeps them forever.

at_desired.description: Collectors whose assignment is the desired version.

FleetVersion.description: A configuration version a fleet runs or should run.

FlowDestination.description: `exporter` is set only on a config-scoped destination, so the UI can label it.

Folder.description: Common folder fields used in HTTP request and response bodies.

icon.description:
Opaque icon token — a Unicode emoji or an "o2:" registry reference.
Absent or null means the folder has no icon.

FolderType.description: Indicates the type of data that the folder can contain; fleets have their own API.

FoundGroup.description: A semantic alias group found in the org's stream schemas.

aliases.description: Actual field name found per stream type, e.g., {"logs": "k8s_cluster_name"}

oneOf.description: Cardinality class derived from unique_values (None if no data yet)

group.description:
Category this group belongs to (e.g., "AWS", "Kubernetes", "Azure", "GCP", "Common").
Sourced from the underlying `FieldAlias.group`. When `None`, the frontend falls
back to inferring the category from `group_id` prefix.

recommended.description:
True if this group appears in 2+ stream types AND has acceptable cardinality
(Deprecated: logic moving to UI)

stream_types.description: Which stream types contain a field from this group (e.g., ["logs", "traces"])

unique_values.description: Number of unique values seen in actual data (None if no data collected yet)

anchor_micros.description: Absent is now, snapped to the last local Monday 00:00 so handovers land on a week boundary.

handover_micros.description: How long one shift lasts, on every shift rule the preset builds. Absent is a week.

new_rotation_name.description: Adds a rotation with this name; setting both fields is a 400.

rotation_id.description: Replaces this rotation's shift rules; its id and name stay.

timezone.description: Absent means the team's own zone; there is no per-user timezone to fall back on.

FromPresetRequest.description: Replaces one rotation's shift rules or adds one; the catalogue says which fields apply.

FunnelDef.description: A funnel as the web's `funnelParam` writes it.

b.description: A built-in key dimension, or any stream column but a session-filter field, env or version.

bs.description: 1-based step an attribute `b` reads its value at; absent lets the data pick it.

FunnelFilter.description: Matches `field` to `values`, inverted by `not`; `f` filters sessions with it, `pc` step events.

GateSettings.description: The verification gate: wait `observe_secs`, then measure over `window_secs`.

GenAiAgentListItem.description: A discovered Gen-AI agent returned by the list endpoint.

env.description: Environment the agent was observed in (e.g. production), when available.

first_seen.description: Epoch-microseconds of the agent's first observed span, when available.

id.description: Stable agent id when source telemetry provided one.

last_seen.description: Epoch-microseconds of the agent's most recent observed span, when available.

name.description: Display name for the agent. Falls back to the agent id when no name is available.

source_stream.description: Source stream where the agent was observed.

source_stream_type.description: Source stream type where the agent was observed.

version.description: Agent (or service) version the agent was observed at, when available.

total.description: Total number of agents after filtering and authorization.

GenAiAgentMappingConfig.description: Org-level fallback mapping for normalizing Gen-AI agent identity.

agent_id_fields.description: Incoming telemetry attribute names to use as fallbacks for `gen_ai.agent.id`.

agent_name_fields.description: Incoming telemetry attribute names to use as fallbacks for `gen_ai.agent.name`.

env_fields.description: Incoming telemetry attribute names to use as fallbacks for the agent's environment.

version_fields.description: Incoming telemetry attribute names to use as fallbacks for the agent's version.

GenerateSqlMetadata.description: Metadata about the generated SQL query.

locked_target_names.description: Display names of the alert's locked workflows and on-call team, by id, for the edit form.

Grade.description:
Day-cell grade, Statuspage-style: one confirmed blip colors a day yellow at
most, never solid red.

Group.description:
One layer's worth of people, for the presets whose layers are fixed. The
name is optional because "the weekend layer" has an obvious label; an empty
one is refused rather than defaulted, because a blank name in a form means
the field was cleared, not skipped.

HaltClass.description: The evidence class of a halt; only the first two may roll back automatically.

HandoffRequest.description: Exactly one of `to` (a person here) or `to_team_id` (the other team's on-call is paged).

model_count.description:
Unpriced check only: every distinct model behind the unpriced spans (spans without a
model name count as one), however many `models` lists.

models.description: Unpriced check only: the 20 models with the most unpriced tokens.

models_truncated.description: Unpriced check only: `models` leaves some of the `model_count` models out.

samples.description: Up to three recent trace ids with the problem; present only with `include_samples`.

unpriced_tokens.description: Unpriced check only: tokens on every unpriced span.

HeatmapYBucket.description: Heatmap y buckets: "size" mode is fixed-width, "log" mode one per power of `base` (2 or 10).

key.description:
Same per-page opaque key as `CurrentComponent.key` — the client join
handle, never the internal component id.

HttpResponse.description:
HTTP response
code 200 is success
code 400 is error
code 404 is not found
code 500 is internal server error
code 503 is service unavailable
code >= 1000 is custom error code
message is the message or error message

hint.description: One-line guidance on how to fix the error (agent self-correction, D4).

suggestions.description: Closest valid alternatives for a mistyped field/function name.

warnings.description:
Problems with a request that succeeded anyway. Distinct from `hint`,
which explains a failure: these accompany a 200, and the caller is
entitled to have meant it.

IdentitySet.description:
One identity set — a disambiguation scheme for one class of workloads.

The `id` is the semantic category slug (e.g. "k8s", "aws", "gcp", "azure").
At processing time the system tries ALL configured sets against each record and
ranks them by coverage of the record's non-empty dimensions: a fully-covered set
wins first, then the highest covered ratio, then the highest raw count; ties are
broken by declaration order (first-in-list). See `resolve_best_set_by_coverage`.

distinguish_by.description: Semantic group IDs used for disambiguation (1..=5).

id.description:
Semantic category slug: "k8s", "aws", "gcp", "azure", or a custom slug.
Must be lowercase, alphanumeric, dash-separated (same rules as FieldAlias IDs).

ImageAttachment.description: Image attachment for multimodal AI chat

Incident.description: Main incident entity - a group of correlated alerts

alert_groups.description: Every alert that fired into the incident and how often, most-fired first; list only.

muted_by_downtime_id.description: Set while a downtime mutes this incident (D3).

oneOf.description:
Latest run summary, `null` when never analyzed; the detail response fills its detail
fields.

rca_off_reason.description: Why automatic analysis runs never start for this incident (`l0_off`).

IncidentAlert.description: Alert info within an incident (junction table representation)

IncidentAlertGroup.description: One alert's firings within an incident, for the list row.

count.description: Times this alert fired into the incident

IncidentMode.description: What a suppressed alert firing does to incidents during the window.

mttr_minutes.description: Mean time to resolve in minutes

IncidentStatus.description: Incident status lifecycle: Open → Acknowledged → Resolved

IncidentTopology.description: Alert flow graph showing how alerts cascaded across services over time

edges.description: Edges showing temporal and service dependency relationships

nodes.description: Alert nodes - each unique (service, alert) pair

composite_alerts.description: Live composite definitions for incident members (`alert_type="composite"`).

triggers.description: Alert triggers (each alert firing is a separate trigger)

IncidentWithAlerts.description: Incident with its alerts (for detail view)

IngestRejection.description: One rejection cause of an org; never holds a secret, a header or body bytes.

first_seen.description: Unix time in microseconds when this reason was first seen; never refreshed.

token.description: Absent for a caller without `incident_integrations` PUT: it ingests into the org.

url.description: Carries the token, so it is withheld with it.

KeyType.description:
Classification of correlation key strength for hierarchical upgrade logic

Hierarchy: AlertId (weakest) → Secondary → Primary (strongest)
Upgrades only move UP the hierarchy, never down.

L0Mode.description: How L0 relates to paging at one severity.

L0Modes.description: Per-severity modes, exactly as the `l0_json` column spells them.

P4.description: Covers P4 and P5 — neither pages a human, so neither has a gate to set.

L0Policy.description:
A team's L0 block. Ships with every auto-created policy, so nobody has to
configure L0 to benefit from it. No `allow_demotion` knob: the ratchet is an
invariant of the engine, not a team preference.

allow_downgrade.description: A `Downgrade` needs `medium` or `high` confidence to ride quieter channels.

allow_suppress.description: Opt-in; when enabled only a `high`-confidence Suppress silences the page.

max_promotion_steps.description:
How far one verdict may raise a severity, so a P4 cannot become a P1 in
a single hop.

LadderStep.description:
One rung: when it fires, and everyone it pages.

The delay identifies the rung, so targets that fire together belong to the
same rung by construction and a ladder cannot show three consecutive rows
all saying "immediately". It also gives the delivery ledger a key that
survives reordering and renaming.

after_micros.description: Delay from `opened_at`, in microseconds. Unique within a rung.

LastRunFields.description: The outcome of a report's latest run and when the next one is due.

last_run_at.description: End of the latest run, Unix µs; null before the first run.

last_run_status.description: succeeded, error or skipped; null before the first run.

next_run_at.description: Due time of the next scheduled run, Unix µs.

LatestSessionsResponse.description:
Session-list pagination deliberately avoids an exact count query because
counting every distinct session is more expensive than fetching one page.
`total` is therefore a lower bound while `has_more` is true, and becomes
exact on the final page.

LeadingEntry.description: One leading hypothesis of the run, as it was led.

can_update_license.description: Whether `POST /license/refresh` would pass both its route check and its handler check.

env_key_in_use.description: Whether the loaded key is the `O2_LICENSE_KEY` one, i.e. no pasted key superseded it.

LinkStatusReport.description: One link's status call: its ranges from the owning querier and its access counters.

LinkSubscriptionRequest.description: Request payload for linking Azure Marketplace subscription

ListAlertsResponseBodyItem.description:
An item in the list returned by the `ListAlerts` endpoint.

`condition` is always present: a concrete query for `scheduled`/`realtime`,
`null` for `composite` and `anomaly_detection` (which have no query). Use
`last_trained_at` and `status` for anomaly state. `trigger_condition` is
present for `scheduled`/`realtime` and omitted otherwise.

oneOf.description: The acks in force on the alert's current firings.
The downtime muting this row now, for the Muted chip. Enterprise only.

child_count.description: Composite rows only: number of referenced children.

destinations.description:
Names of the notification destinations this alert delivers to
(`Alert.destinations`). Lets the destination↔alert dependency view build
the linkage from the list alone; omitted when empty.

expression_summary.description: Composite rows only: the trigger expression with child IDs resolved to names.

firing_started_at.description: Start of the alert's current firing (µs); absent when not firing or for a multi-alert.

groups_firing.description:
Multi-alerts only: how many of those groups were warning-or-worse,
also counted pre-cap. With `groups_observed` this is the "N of M groups
firing" chip. Counting retained state rows instead would silently
under-report whenever more than the cap's worth of groups fire, which
is the silent truncation M-6 forbids.

groups_firing_is_lower_bound.description:
Whether `groups_firing` is a `>=` lower bound. Tracked separately
because the two diverge: a full page that still reached healthy groups
has seen every firing group, so this stays exact while
`groups_observed` does not.

groups_observed.description:
Multi-alerts only (§5.4): how many groups the last evaluation observed,
counted **before** the M-6 cap truncated them. Absent for every alert
that has not opted in.

groups_observed_is_lower_bound.description:
Whether `groups_observed` is a `>=` lower bound — the bounded fetch
page came back full, so groups beyond it were never seen. Render the
count with a `≥`.

oneOf.description: The open incident the current firing belongs to. Enterprise only.

last_error.description: Last error message from training or detection. Only present for `anomaly_detection` items.

last_outcome.description:
Outcome of the most recent evaluation: "firing" | "normal" | "error" |
"notify_failed" | "succeeded". Absent when the alert has never run.

This is the LAST RUN OUTCOME, not a live "currently firing" flag —
always render it alongside `last_outcome_at`. See Part IV of alerts.md.

last_outcome_since.description:
When `last_outcome` last CHANGED (microseconds) — i.e. how long the
alert has been in its current state.

last_trained_at.description:
Timestamp (µs) when the anomaly model was last successfully trained.
Only present for `anomaly_detection` items.

level.description:
Severity of the last classification: "ok" | "warning" | "critical".

A SEPARATE axis from `last_outcome`: that says whether the evaluation
fired, this says how bad. An alert can be `firing` at `warning`.
Absent for single-level alerts that never classified.

level_since.description: When `level` last CHANGED — powers "critical for 20 minutes".

oncall_team.description:
The on-call team this alert names, when it names one.

Routing's highest-precedence tier, and the only tier a list row can
report: every other one resolves from the identity dimensions of the row
that fires, which an alert definition does not carry. Absent means
"resolved at fire time", not "pages nobody".

The list has always had a column for this and never had the field, so
every alert read as unbound — including ones deliberately pinned.

priority.description:
Configured priority as the integer storage id 1..=5 (Feature 2, PT-3).

A THIRD axis: `enabled` is is-it-running, `last_outcome` is
did-it-fire, `level` is how-bad-now, and this is how much humans care.
Absent when unset, which is every pre-Feature-2 alert.

referenced_by_composite_count.description: Count of parent composites currently readable to the caller.

status.description:
Scheduler status string. Only present for `anomaly_detection` items.
Values: "waiting" | "ready" | "training" | "failed" | "disabled"

stream_name.description:
The stream this alert watches. Absent for `composite` alerts (which
watch children, not a stream) and for an `anomaly_detection` config
that predates stream selection.

stream_type.description: Paired with `stream_name` — present and absent together.

tags.description: Normalized selection tags (PT-6). Omitted when empty.

template.description:
Alert-level template override (`Alert.template`): when set it replaces the
destination-level template for every destination above. Absent when the
alert defers to each destination's own template.

ListDashboardsResponseBodyItem.description: An item in the list returned by the `ListDashboards` endpoint.

ListRcaRunsQuery.description: Query parameters for listing an incident's analysis runs

before.description: Return runs older than this run id (the last run of the previous page)

provider.description: Billing provider: "stripe", "aws", or "azure". Omitted for external-contract subs.

LlmScoreAnnotationSource.description:
How an annotation was submitted.

The distinction is whether a review submission governed it, not which page
it was typed on: Discovery is where a target is found and queued, so an
annotation made there is a direct one, the same as any other.

LlmScoreErrorReason.description:
Producer identity used to build the read-side deduplication key.
Why an errored Score carries no value.

The mirror of `skip_reason`: that explains a `Skipped` status, this explains
an `Error` one. Terminality is a scalar comparison on this column, so
deciding whether a scorer is finished never depends on parsing a JSON blob.

LlmScoreRecord.description:
Open-ended JSON fields are stored as one string column each.

Log ingestion flattens nested values before schema inference. A plain
`Option<Value>` field therefore becomes one column per key, no parent key
survives a `SELECT *`, and every key a scorer invents widens the stream
schema permanently. `evaluation_key` already avoids this by being a
`String`. Any field added here that holds open-ended JSON needs the same
`serde_as` attribute.

annotation_metadata.description:
Open-ended metadata the annotation request attached to the annotation as
a whole. Set only on the annotation path.

attempt_count.description:
Attempts this scorer dimension has consumed, 1-based. Resuming the
bounded sequence after a restart reads this and nothing else.

client_reported.description:
True when the customer's own code produced this Score and reported it
through the SDK. A client Score never carries a Scorer reference, so
this is what separates it from a platform Score in every query.

client_scorer_key.description:
Stable client-supplied identity for one local scorer. It separates
multiple client dimensions that bind the same Score Config.

input_preview.description: Bounded excerpt of the target input the scorer evaluated.

input_span_id.description: Span the scorer read the target input from, when it came from one span.

oneOf.description:
Original scorer provenance before an Experiment wraps the score in its
own queryable source type. Older records omit this field.

output_preview.description: Bounded excerpt of the target output the scorer evaluated.

output_span_id.description: Span the scorer read the target output from, when it came from one span.

queue_id.description:
Queue provenance for Workbench review Scores. Together with
`review_submission_id`, these fields make `_llm_scores` independently
queryable without a relational Review or Review Score table.

reasoning.description: Justification for this individual Score dimension.

record_ts.description:
`_timestamp` of the Experiment execution record being scored. A score
is fresh only while this still matches the latest execution record.

ref_timestamp.description:
Timestamp of the evaluated span, trace, or session. This stays distinct
from `_timestamp`, which records when the Score itself was written.

review_submission_comments.description:
Overall comment for the complete Review Submission. Annotation
projection repeats this value on each Score in the submission.

review_submission_id.description: Logical N/N grouping key for authoritative annotation-source Scores.

review_submission_score_count.description:
Distinct physical Score Config rows required for this complete N/N
review submission.

score_config_row_id.description:
Physical immutable Score Config row used for this Score. Queue reviews
use it to prove exact N/N rubric coverage.

scorer_metadata.description:
Open-ended metadata that whatever produced this Score's value attached
to it: LLM judge output, remote scorer output, or a reviewer's per-Score
metadata. Never interpreted by the server.

oneOf.description: Permanent reason this dimension was intentionally not scored.

target_scope.description: Canonical evaluated target identity for latest-score grouping.

task_trigger_reason.description:
Free-text reason a person gave when triggering a manual evaluation.
Distinct from `reasoning`, which is the scorer's justification for the
value it produced.

LlmScoreStatus.description:
Outcome of one scorer dimension for one target.

Older score records predate this field, so successful scoring remains the
deserialization default.

LocationAgentInfo.description:
A registered agent as shown on the location detail page (read-only —
agents self-register; there is nothing to edit).

LocationCheckSummary.description: One synthetic assigned to the location, for the detail page's checks table.

install.description: Install command for private rows; withheld without PUT on the default folder.

LocationDetail.description:
`GET /{org}/synthetics/locations/{id}` — the location entry (same stats as
the list) plus its agents and assigned checks.

LocationEntry.description:
One location as returned by `GET /{org}/synthetics/locations` — a superset
of the legacy env-derived shape (`id`/`name`/`region`/`provider`) plus
registry fields and computed per-type availability.

agent_names.description:
Names of the live agents (most recently seen first) — shown as subtext
in the check form's private-location rows.

checks_count.description: Synthetics in the caller's org that run from this location.

checks_per_min.description: Σ 60/interval_secs over the enabled synthetics above.

label.description: Display label — user/agent-chosen (private) or o2's friendly name (public).

live_agents.description: Number of live agents serving this location.

live_status_unknown.description:
True when `status` is this region's best guess rather than an
observation — see [`resolve_live_status`].

Additive on purpose. Widening `status` itself with a fourth value would
break every client that switches on it: the locations table renders
`t("synthetics.privateLocations.status." + status)`, so an unrecognised
value shows the raw key path, and the check form's tier mapping treats
"not online and not pending" as offline — the exact false alarm this
exists to remove. An unknown field is ignored instead.

Skipped when false, so a deployment without super cluster serves a
byte-identical payload to the one it served before this field existed.

status.description:
"online" (any live agent; public rows always), "offline" (agents
registered but all stale), "pending" (private row, nothing registered).

types.description:
Check types runnable at this location (computed: base set for public
rows, live agents' self-reported capabilities for private rows).

version.description: Binary version of the most recently seen agent.

LockoutBackoff.description: How lockout duration grows with each successive lockout.

bucket_size.description: Failed attempts before each subsequent lockout. `0` reuses `threshold`.

threshold.description: Failed attempts before the first lockout. `0` disables lockout entirely.

LockoutState.description:
A user's lockout state as an administrator sees it.

The counters and the escalation level are included because the reader is an authenticated
instance admin. They must not be handed to the user they describe: someone who can read the
level and the remaining seconds can derive the thresholds behind them and pace attempts to stay
underneath.

lockout_level.description:
How many lockouts this account has served. Kept after a lock expires, because it is what
makes the next one longer.

retry_after_secs.description: Seconds until the account may try again, present only while the lock holds.

LokiEntry.description: Loki log entry containing timestamp, message, and optional metadata

structured_metadata.description: Optional structured metadata as key-value pairs

timestamp.description: Timestamp as nanosecond unix epoch string (e.g., "1609459200000000000")

LokiPushRequest.description:
Internal Loki JSON types for native Loki push API format
Loki push request - matches native JSON format exactly

streams.description: Array of log streams, each containing labels and log entries

LokiPushResponse.description: Loki Push Response (for documentation only - actual responses are 204 No Content or plain text)

LokiStream.description: Loki stream containing labels and log entries

values.description: Array of log entries, each containing timestamp, message, and optional structured metadata

MarkArea.description: Shaded band on a cartesian chart; `axis` is "x" or "y", `from`/`to` are axis values as strings.

snooze_hours.description:
Hours to snooze the underlying check org-wide (default 6, per mockup
B1's "snooze 6h").

MarkLookup.description: Whether the caller's protection lookup answered; only `Ok` lets `protected` reach the gate.

MarkReadRequest.description: `all` is the "clear my inbox" button and is bounded server-side.

read.description: `false` puts them back to unread: a 3am dismissal by accident must be undoable.

MatchKind.description: How an object was matched when no query referencing the metric could be parsed.

MatchOp.description: How a rule value is compared with a field: `in` lists every value, the rest take one each.

nights.description: How many of those arrived between 22:00 and 06:00 in the team's zone.

pages.description:
Pages sent to them — counted off the delivery ledger, so a firing that
climbed three rungs counts once for each of the three people it reached.

MemberReachability.description: What would happen if the ladder tried to reach one person right now.

channels.description: Every channel, with its verdict. The UI's row of chips.

configured_but_unverified.description: Methods on file that no transport may use — `phone`, `push`.

deliverable_channels.description: Channels that could carry a page to this person today.

is_org_user.description:
The address resolves to a user of this organization. When false, nothing
else can be true: there is no inbox, no login, and no way for this person
to acknowledge anything.

mailbox_shaped.description:
The address is shaped like a mailbox. `root@example` and `admin` are
both perfectly valid OpenObserve logins and neither can receive mail.

why_not.description: Why a page would not land. `None` when it would.

would_a_page_land.description:
The one boolean the badge renders. True iff at least one channel could
deliver.

MentionRule.description: Who a repeat or a level-up mentions; `Default` is `@here` for critical and nobody otherwise.

MetricUsage.description: The objects that use a metric, and how many unparseable queries name it.

unparsed.description: Queries that name the metric but could not be parsed, so matched only as text.

ModelPricingDefinition.description: A model pricing definition that maps model names (via regex) to pricing tiers.

children.description:
Definitions shadowed by this one (same match_pattern, lower source/sort priority).
Only populated in list responses — not stored in the database.

description.description: Human-readable description. Populated for built-in entries.

match_pattern.description:
Regex pattern to match model names from incoming spans.
Example: "(?i)^gpt-4o" or "(?i)^(claude-sonnet-4-6)$"
Max length: 512 characters.

name.description: Display name for the model (e.g., "GPT-4o", "Claude Sonnet 4.6")

provider.description: Provider name (e.g., "OpenAI", "Anthropic"). Populated for built-in entries.

sort_order.description:
Explicit sort order for deterministic tie-breaking when multiple definitions match the
same model name and have equal (or absent) `valid_from` values.
Lower values are checked first; the first match wins.
Defaults to 0 — set a lower number to make a definition take priority.

oneOf.description: Ownership source: built_in (synced from GitHub), meta_org, or org.

tiers.description: Pricing tiers; `ranks_tiers()` decides between first-match and highest-rank selection.

valid_from.description:
Optional Unix timestamp (microseconds) from which this definition is valid.
When multiple definitions match the same model name, the one with the
greatest `valid_from` that is still <= the span's start time is used.
If None, the definition is valid for all time.

model.description: Null for spans that carry no model name.

alert_ids.description: IDs of the alerts to move.

anomaly_config_ids.description:
IDs of anomaly detection configs to move. Defaults to empty when not
provided. Callers should always supply this to avoid per-ID DB lookups.

dst_folder_id.description: Indicates the folder to which alerts should be moved.

dashboard_ids.description: IDs of the dashboards to move.

dst_folder_id.description: Indicates the folder to which dashboard should be moved.

workflow_ids.description: IDs of the workflows to move.

advisory.description: Human/agent-readable note about server-side formatting decisions.

data.description: Formatted result block when `format` is set; `hits` is emptied.

format.description:
Set when `agent_options.output_format` reformatted `hits` into `data`:
"csv", "md_table", or "ndjson" (automatic fallback for sparse results).

hits.description: Rows, or with `per_query_response` one array of values per query

MuteSource.description: Where a quick mute came from; the web app's own calls are `openobserve`.

MutedPage.description: One page a mute snoozed until it ends; `refused` says why it was not.

NamedEventRef.description: A deleted named event's id and the name it had when it was deleted.

id.description: Unique identifier for the node (use UUID format)

io_type.description:
Node role in the pipeline. MUST be one of:
- "input": Source stream node (first node in pipeline)
- "output": Destination stream node (last node in pipeline)
- "default": Processing node (function, condition, etc.)

NotAvailableReason.description: Why a panel is withheld; deliberately generic, it never names a stream on the public plane.

NoticeAdminView.description:
Admin view of a notice: unlike [`PublicNotice`], this carries the internal
id and mapped component ids the edit UI needs to round-trip — it must
never be reachable from the public plane.

ObjectUsage.description: An SLO or scheduled pipeline whose query reads the metric.

oneOf.description: `text` when only an unparseable query names the metric; absent for a parsed match.

OnCallPosition.description:
Who one rotation puts on call at an instant.

One per rotation, and only a rotation produces one — so a position cannot
appear here because something derived it rather than because it is staffed.

next_user_email.description:
Who takes over at the next handover.

Display only — nothing pages this. It once doubled as the secondary,
which is how one team got two different people both correctly labelled
"the secondary".

override_id.description: Set when a cover, rather than a shift rule, put this person here.

rotation_id.description: The rotation's id. What a level of the escalation policy points at.

rotation_name.description: The rotation's name, for a human reading a page or a calendar.

rule.description: Which shift rule inside it produced this answer.

OnCallResponse.description: The record itself, as the API and the UI see it.

oneOf.description:
Why it happened, captured at resolve — the history the next firing of
this rule reads.

cause_note.description:
The sentence beside the structured cause. One dropdown plus one line is
the whole ask — anything longer does not get filled in at 3am.

exhausted_at.description:
When the ladder ran out with nobody answering. `None` while it is still
climbing, or if somebody took it first.

Deliberately NOT a `ResponseState`. An exhausted page can still be
acknowledged and resolved, so a lifecycle state would force a false
either/or: exhaustion is a property of the ladder, the state is a
property of the human.

incident_id.description:
Set only when this firing also produced an incident. A record is never
owned by an incident, so this stays `None` for most firings.

ladder_anchor.description: Where step delays count from: `opened_at`, moved by a snooze or a triage-held first page.

ladder_run.description:
Which run of the ladder the record is on.

Handing a page to another person or team starts a new run, and the ledger
is read per run — which is what makes the receiving responder's ladder
begin at its first rung. Absent means the first run.

origin_response_id.description: For an impacted record, the owner record it was opened alongside.

priority.description: `AlertPriority::to_i32` — the same scale alerts already use.

snoozed_until.description:
Quiet until this instant, in micros.

Not an acknowledgement: snoozing says "I know, stop shouting", not "I
have this". The record stays open and unowned and the ladder resumes when
it expires — which is what makes it safe to offer.

team_id.description:
The team that owns this firing, or `None` when routing found nobody.

A teamless record pages nobody — no policy, no rotation, no ladder — and
exists so the firing appears beside the ones that did page. Handing it to
a team gives it an owner and starts its ladder (R-D6).

title.description:
What the page is about. Kept on the record so it survives the alert
being renamed or deleted.

updated_at.description:
Revision of the write this record came from, and what a replica accepts
or refuses a snapshot on. The queue redelivers an unacked message behind
newer ones, so a blind apply lets an older snapshot un-acknowledge a
page that a human already answered.

OpenQuestion.description: The question a paused run waits on.

created_at.description: When the organization was created, as a Unix timestamp in microseconds; 0 when unknown.

owner_email.description:
The org admin/owner's email — used by the frontend to disambiguate
two orgs that share a display name (e.g. two orgs both named
"default"). Empty when no admin could be resolved (e.g. root-user
view of a stale org).

owner_first_name.description:
The org admin/owner's first name, when set; the frontend falls back
to the local part of `owner_email` when this is empty.

OrgMetricUsage.description: Usage counts for each current metric stream that visible objects read; other names are dropped.

OrgPublicDashboardSettings.description: The org's settings as the settings API has them; a null `max_links` is the env default.

OrgTelephonyView.description: The org's own account without its token.

partial_coverage.description:
True when some trace streams could not be searched (no index, no
permission, or indexing disabled), so `not_found` is not org-wide proof.

name.description: Only alphanumeric characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9), spaces, and underscores are allowed

service_account.description:
Optional service account email to add to the organization
When specified, only this service account will be added (not the API caller)

ai_rca_thread_tool_output.description: Show raw tool input and output in incident investigation threads.

scrape_interval.description:
Ideally this should be the same as prometheus-scrape-interval (in
seconds).

resolved_data_retention.description: The default each stream type resolves to here, computed on read and never stored.

OtlpProtobufBody.description: The protobuf-encoded `Export*ServiceResponse`, sent when the request was protobuf.

OutcomeReason.description: The rule that set the outcome.

OwnershipRule.description: A team's claim over part of the identity space.

dimensions.description:
Every pair that must match for this rule to apply. An empty map is a
catch-all and is rejected by [`Self::validate`] — an accidental one
would silently capture every alert in the org.

A value may end in `*` to claim the subtree below a literal prefix
(`host=db-*`), which §7 asks for on deployments whose finest dimension
is a numbered host rather than a namespace.

last_matched_at.description: Micros. `None` when it has never matched.

total.description: Rules matching the filter, before paging.

PageAdminView.description:
Admin view of a page. Deliberately omits `password_hash`; carries only
whether a password is set.

components.description:
Populated only by the detail GET (not the list), so the edit UI can
render and round-trip the existing component→check mapping.

oneOf.description: Live health summary for the list view (worst component status).

PageOp.description: How an ignored-page rule compares its value with a page key.

PageRule.description: Takes `PageOp`, not `ViewOp`, because `param` and `ref` mean nothing on a page key.

PaginatedResponse.description: Paginated response used by list-style APIs (sessions, traces, users).

PaidOverageBillingStatus.description: Billing eligibility attached to cumulative paid-overage state.

PaidOverageOrganizationStatus.description: One organization's cumulative authorization state for a quota feature.

PaidOverageStatus.description: Public cumulative state. Internal feature-row keys are intentionally absent.

duplicate.description: Accepted without writing: this part was already stored as submitted.

PartitionTimeLevelChange.description: From `since`, a UTC day start in microseconds, the stream's days are at `level`.

PasswordComplexity.description:
The subset of the policy safe to show a non-admin: what a password must look like, and nothing
about how the instance defends itself.

Lockout thresholds and history depth are deliberately absent. A brute-forcer who can read
`lockout.threshold` and `lockout.start_secs` knows exactly how to pace attempts to stay under
them, which turns a defence into a published rate limit.

special_char_set.description: Empty means any non-alphanumeric character counts as special.

apply_to_root.description:
Whether root is held to rotation and lockout like every other native user.

Default `false`, which is the documented exemption: root is the only account that can
repair a misconfigured policy, and the only one whose lockout has no remedy from inside
the product. Complexity and reuse already apply to root at password-set time whatever
this says; the tightening sweep never touches root either way, so root is never
mass-flagged.

cookie_max_age_secs.description:
How long a sign-in cookie stays valid, in seconds. `0` defers to `ZO_COOKIE_MAX_AGE`.

This is the browser's copy of the credential, not a server-side session: shortening it
makes the browser stop sending the cookie sooner, and does nothing to a copy taken from
it. It applies from the next sign-in — cookies already issued keep the lifetime they
were given.

history_max_retained.description:
Hashes retained per user; kept at or above `history_count` so a later increase to
`history_count` has history to check against.

max_length.description: Between `min_length` and 128; a stored legacy `0` still reads as unbounded.

rotation_warning_days.description:
Days before expiry to start warning. `0` = never warn; equal to `rotation_days` = warn on
every request, since no live password is then outside the window.

special_char_set.description: Empty means any non-alphanumeric character counts as special.

Pipeline.description: One `service.pipelines` entry of a fleet; collectors on older versions add to the same name.

in_rate.description: Items per second over the window; null means no telemetry, 0 a measured zero.

queue_ratio.description: The fullest exporter queue over the last 45s.

dropped.description: Items per second that failed to enqueue over the last 5m.

failed.description: Items per second that failed to send over the last 5m.

PipelineFleet.description: A readable fleet; without telemetry it lists its stable (else desired) version's pipelines.

PipelineKind.description:
Distinguishes user-created pipelines from system-managed evaluation pipelines.

- `User` pipelines are visible in the Pipeline UI and subject to the "one realtime pipeline per
  stream" constraint.
- `Evaluation` pipelines are hidden from the Pipeline UI, managed exclusively by the Online Eval
  subsystem, and any number can coexist with a user pipeline on the same stream.

refused.description: Refused items per second over the last 5m.

PipelineSource.description:
Pipeline source type determines when the pipeline runs.
Use "realtime" for processing data as it arrives, "scheduled" for periodic batch processing.

allOf.description:
Real-time pipeline: processes data immediately as it's ingested.
Example: { "source_type": "realtime" }

oneOf.description:
Real-time pipeline: processes data immediately as it's ingested.
Example: { "source_type": "realtime" }

metrics_restricted.description: Some throughput queries were skipped because the caller may not read their metric streams.

PlanPreview.description: The expanded plan for the fleet's current size.

collapsed.description: The first batch covers every eligible collector, so the plan is one batch.

params.description:
Sampling parameters, passed to the provider verbatim. `temperature` and
`max_tokens` are read out for the provider's own fields; the rest ride
through untouched, which is how a caller reaches provider-specific
options without a schema change here.

tools.description:
Tool definitions, passed through. A tool call comes back as the cell's
output; nothing is executed.

content.description:
Structured content is accepted and passed through, so multimodal and
tool-result messages survive.

input.description: A string binds `{{input}}`; an object binds each of its fields by name.

ladder_is_generated.description: Still the shape this code wrote, so dropping a rotation rewrites it rather than refusing.

PolicyView.description: A team's escalation policy as the API returns it.

PoolUsageResponse.description:
One pool's usage for an org. Field names are unit-neutral because AI counts
credits and synthetics counts steps.

pool.description: Stable pool identifier — one of [`TrialQuotaPool::ALL_POOLS`]' keys.

is_external.description: Is the user created via ldap flow.

description.description: One line: what applying it builds.

layers.description:
The layers it generates, highest priority first, in the same words the
generated schedule will use.

name.description: What to call it on a button.

PresetId.description: Which preset. Serialises to the id the catalogue publishes.

PresetInput.description: One field of a preset's request body.

default.description: What the server uses when the field is absent, already in wire shape.

field.description: The JSON key, exactly as the request body spells it.

fields.description: For `group` and `group_list`: the fields each group carries.

label.description: What to put beside the control.

PresetInputKind.description:
What kind of control a field is. Enough for a form to be generated rather
than hardcoded — the UI should not have to know that `follow_the_sun` wants
between two and four groups, because then it would have to be told twice.

PresetSpec.description:
The inputs of one preset, tagged by which preset they are for.

Internally tagged on `preset`, so the wire shape is §C.3's. Each variant
names its layers rather than taking a positional array: "which of these two
groups is the weekend one" is exactly the question a positional API leaves
open until somebody is paged on a Saturday.

oneOf.description: Two to four regional layers over one catch-all.

Who covers the hours no region claims. Absent means everybody named
above, in the order they were named — what a follow-the-sun team
almost always wants and never has to think about.
A Mon–Fri layer over a weekend layer.
The week cut at one boundary, each half to a group.

boundary_minute.description: Minutes from midnight in the team's timezone. Defaults to 00:00.

first.description: Covers from Monday 00:00 up to the boundary.

second.description: Covers from the boundary to the end of the week.

oneOf.description: A working-hours layer over an out-of-hours catch-all.

end_minute.description: Minutes from midnight in the team's timezone, exclusive. 17:00.

start_minute.description: Minutes from midnight in the team's timezone, inclusive. 09:00.

available.description:
Whether this deployment can actually run the agent.

Same honesty rule the channel list follows: a policy naming a thing that
cannot happen is worse than one that does not name it, because the screen
reads as configured. A `gate` with no agent reachable does not hold the
page — it pages immediately — and this is what lets the screen say so.

mode.description:
`parallel` | `gate` | `only` | `off`, already resolved for this
priority — so a caller never re-derives the P1 invariant or the
pages-nobody rule.

triage_budget_seconds.description: How long a `gate` holds the page waiting for a verdict.

applies.description: SLOs on the detail page: false when the current or next window holds no slice start.

body_html.description: Server-rendered markdown; the FE sanitizes with dompurify.

PreviewRecipient.description: One person a rung would reach, and whether the page would land.

reason.description: Why this rung names them — "you are on call".

PreviewResolvedScheduleRequest.description: An unsaved rotation and the window to resolve it over, in micros.

PreviewRoutingRequest.description: Resolves the same rules a real firing would and sends nothing.

PreviewRung.description: One rung, resolved against right now.

resolves_to_nobody.description:
The rung resolves to nobody at this instant. The single most important
thing this endpoint can say.

targets.description: What the rung says, before resolution — `the on-call`, `ana@o2.ai`.

PreviousResult.description: The newest usable result of an earlier run.

PricingMatchKind.description:
How a pricing pattern matched a model name.

Ordered so that `Exact > Approximate`: when several patterns of the same source match, an exact
match wins.

PricingRuleRef.description: The name and source of a pricing rule.

PricingSource.description: Ownership source of a model pricing definition.

PricingTierDefinition.description: A pricing tier within a model definition.

oneOf.description:
Optional condition that must be met for this tier to apply.
If None, this is the default (fallback) tier.

name.description: Display name for this tier (e.g., "Default", "Extended Context")

prices.description:
Prices per token, keyed by usage type.
Keys must exactly match usage keys produced by the span extractor:
  "input", "output", "cache_read_input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", etc.
Values are price per single token (e.g., 0.000003 = $3/1M tokens).

**Precision note:** `f64` provides ~15 significant decimal digits, which is more
than sufficient for cost *estimation* on observability data. These values are not
used for billing or financial accounting — they produce approximate cost figures
for dashboards and alerts. The multiplication `token_count as f64 * price` is
exact for token counts < 2^53 (~9 quadrillion), well beyond practical span sizes.

priority.description: Breaks ties between matching tiers before the restriction count; higher wins.

rules.description: Span-attribute rules (service tier, speed, region) that must all hold.

utc_windows.description:
Recurring UTC time-of-day windows during which this tier applies.

Empty (the default) means the tier is not time-restricted. Providers such as
DeepSeek publish "peak" and "off-peak" rates that repeat every day, which is a
time-of-day range rather than an absolute cutover (that is what `valid_from` is
for). A tier applies when the span falls in ANY of its windows *and* its
`condition` (if set) passes, so windows compose with context-length tiering.

PriorityRung.description: One priority's ladder and channel set.

channels.description:
Applies to everyone paged at this priority — the primary and the
secondary are not treated differently.

steps.description: Empty means this priority never pages a human.

ProblemAckRequest.description: The optional body of the page and incident acknowledge routes.

baseline.description: The "before" query; same fields as a merge request.

comparison.description: The "after" query; `profile_type` and `profile_unit` must match the baseline.

baseline_total.description: Baseline total over all its stacks; above `root.before_total` when `truncated`.

comparison_total.description: Comparison total over all its stacks; above `root.total` when `truncated`.

root.description: Call tree: `total` / `self` are the comparison side, `before_*` the baseline.

top.description: One row per function from both sides, largest share change first (pre-truncation).

tree_truncated.description: True when the call tree was cut to `max_nodes` and light nodes folded into `other`.

truncated.description: True when either side exceeded the unique-stack limit.

merged_total.description: Sample weight represented in `root` / `top` after the unique-stack cap.

top.description: Flattened top functions by exclusive (`self`) value (pre-truncation).

total.description: Full sample weight in scope (from `sum(value)` when stacks were capped).

tree_truncated.description: True when the call tree was cut to `max_nodes` and light nodes folded into `other`.

truncated.description: True when unique stacks exceeded the query size limit.

group_by.description: Label column that splits `series` into `groups` (series endpoint only).

group_limit.description: Groups returned before the rest fold into one `others` group: 1..=50, default 10.

start_time.description: Missing reads as 0 so `parse_required_time_range` reports it, not the JSON parser.

others.description: True for the single group that sums every value past `group_limit`.

value.description: Label value; "" when rows lack the label, and for the `others` group.

rate.description: Value per second of profiled time, summed over instances; CPU ns / 1e9 = cores.

groups.description: Only when `group_by` is set: top `group_limit` values by total, then one `others` group.

series.description: Sum over all groups per bucket.

group.description: The OR group the matcher belongs to; absent means the base list every group is ANDed with.

negate.description: Set on every matcher of a negated group.

PromoteRequest.description: Promotes a firing to a full incident.

severity.description: Absent derives it from the record's priority, so a promotion cannot silently downgrade.

title.description: Absent takes the record's own title, which is one less field to fill in mid-page.

ProviderRequestBody.description: HTTP request body for creating/updating a Provider.

ProviderResponseBody.description: HTTP response body for a Provider (auth_config masked).

authConfigMasked.description: API key / auth config is masked in responses.

endpoint.description: Null for a provider on the built-in default, so the form field stays empty.

resolvedEndpoint.description: The URL actually called, with the default filled in when `endpoint` is null.

PublicDashboardConfig.description: Admin body to create or update a link; variables stay frozen at the author's values.

name.description: Label that tells a dashboard's links apart; empty is allowed.

PublicDashboardTimeRange.description: One window a link offers: rolling and refreshed on read, or fixed and built once.

oneOf.description: UTC micros.

PublicDashboardVisibility.description: Draft configures the share without exposing it; Public serves it and is the default.

PublicLinkStatus.description: A link's state as the admin UI shows it; `NeedsAttention` comes from the batch status call.

PublicLinkView.description: A link as the admin API returns it; the slug is a bearer secret for authenticated routes only.

publisher_left.description: The publisher is no longer an org member; the link may still be enabled while cleanup lags.

slug.description: Null when the caller cannot read the link's dashboard.

updates.description:
The "investigating / mitigated / resolved" narrative timeline, oldest
first. No internal update id — same IDOR reasoning as the notice.

PutAppSettings.description: The body of a settings PUT: the built-in bot switch, session rules and ignored pages.

version.description: 0 creates; any other must equal the stored version.

PutTelephonyRequest.description: A missing or blank `auth_token` keeps the stored one; no `Debug`, since it carries the token.

key.description:
Numeric: bucket index, usable as `bucket_from` / `bucket_to` on the
Scores list. Boolean / categorical: the value, usable as `value`.

lower.description: Numeric only: inclusive lower edge. Bucket 0 also holds values below it.

unhealthy.description: `None` when the config has no healthy threshold.

upper.description:
Numeric only: exclusive upper edge. The last bucket also holds values
at or above it.

scopeCounts.description:
Counts for every scope, ignoring the `scope` filter, so the UI can
render the scope toggle.

oneOf.description:
Boolean and categorical configs: the most frequent value. Ties go to
the smaller value.

unhealthy.description: `None` when the config has no healthy threshold.

inputSpanId.description:
Span the scorer read the input from: the stored id, or `span_id` for a
span Score. `None` for older trace and session Scores.

outputSpanId.description: Span the scorer read the output from, with the same fallback.

refTimestamp.description:
Start time of the scored span, trace or session, in microseconds. Use
it, not `timestamp`, to open the target. Older Scores without it fall
back to `timestamp`.

unhealthy.description: `None` when the config has no healthy threshold.

value.description: Number, boolean or string, following the config data type.

QualityTimelineBucket.description: Latest Scores written in one slice of the time range.

average.description: Numeric configs only; `None` for a bucket without Scores.

end.description: Exclusive bucket end, in microseconds. The last one ends at `end_time`.

start.description:
Inclusive bucket start, in microseconds. Buckets align to multiples of
their width, so the first one starts at `start_time`, not earlier.

trueCount.description: Boolean configs only: Scores with the value `true`.

unhealthy.description: `None` when the config has no healthy threshold.

promql_multi_alert.description:
Per-group alerting for a PromQL alert (M-9), where a "group" is one
returned SERIES.

A sibling of `promql_condition` rather than a member of
[`Aggregation::multi_alert`], because a PromQL alert has no
`aggregation` at all — its grouping is expressed in the PromQL itself
(`sum by (pod) (…)`), not in a `group_by` column list.

The group key is the series' FULL label set. That is what a series'
identity already is in Prometheus, and it means the expression stays
the single place grouping is decided — a separate label picker could
only ever disagree with the `by (…)` clause beside it.

`#[serde(default)]` carries the same backward-compatibility guarantee
as its aggregation counterpart: an alert stored before this field
existed deserializes to `false` and keeps its collapsed evaluation
byte-for-byte. Nothing is inferred from the query returning several
series — that would change paging cadence for every existing PromQL
alert that happens to be unaggregated.

promql_warning_value.description:
WARNING value for the PromQL condition (alerts_2.md Feature 1).

A sibling field rather than a member of `Condition`, which is shared by
every filter in the product and must not grow alert-specific knobs.
Shares `promql_condition.operator` with critical. `None` = single-level.

Lenient deserialization: this arrives through
`CreateAlertRequestBody`'s `#[serde(flatten)]`, which buffers via
`Value`, where `arbitrary_precision` makes a number a map (D61).
Without it a FRACTIONAL warning is rejected while an integer one works
— found by end-to-end testing.

oneOf.description:

Why a page turned out to happen.

jobs, so they get different records, and each team acks and resolves its own.

A named position, and the only thing here that puts a person on call.

Zenduty's *schedule*, incident.io's *rota*. Resolves to exactly one person

The stack. Highest priority whose restrictions match at `at` wins, and
exactly one does.

Carried on the schedule rather than fetched at each call site because

Org-level service identity configuration.

Contains 1–5 identity sets. Service name is always derived from the "service"
semantic group — hardcoded, not configurable.

At processing time each record is matched against ALL sets and ranked by
coverage of the record's non-empty dimensions: full coverage > highest ratio >
highest count, ties broken by declaration order. The same ranking is used on the
correlation read path so ingest files records under the set reads will select.
If no set has any coverage the record is skipped.

When true, correlation matches streams to services without requiring the `service`
dimension. Useful when some streams (e.g. metrics) lack `service.name` but share
infrastructure attributes (e.g. `k8s-namespace`) with streams that do (e.g. logs).

correlated bucket. Defaults to false (current behavior preserved).

A tightening write forces a password reset on every affected user, so the count comes back with
the policy rather than leaving the admin to discover the blast radius from support tickets.

A narrower rule, belonging to another team, that takes pages this rule would
otherwise catch.

Deliberately not "another rule claims the same path". That state cannot
exist: `idx_oncall_ownership_org_path` is unique on `(org_id, path)`, so a
second claim is a 409 at write time. What does happen is a deeper or more
exact rule quietly absorbing the firings somebody expected this rule to
take — worth saying only when the deeper rule belongs to a different team,
because within one team it changes nothing about who gets woken.
