Instant at which `members[0]`'s first shift begins, in microseconds.

Shifts before it resolve too — the sequence extends backwards — so an
anchor in the future is not an error.

This is the whole "secondary" mechanism. Two rotations with the same
roster and anchors one shift apart can never resolve to the same
person, and that is data, not a rule: nothing at resolution time knows
they are related.

The rule stops applying at or after this instant. `None` means "until
further notice".

How a rule is retired (`architecture/02` §3b). Deleting it instead
would throw away the record of who covered those hours. Exclusive, like
every boundary here.

Participants in handover order. Emails, because email is the login and
therefore the one identifier every user is guaranteed to have.

What this rule is called on the calendar. "APAC business hours",
"Weekend", "Base rotation".

Higher wins when two rules in the same rotation both apply.

Explicit rather than positional, so reordering the UI list cannot
silently change who gets paged.

When this rule applies. Empty means always — the catch-all every
follow-the-sun setup needs underneath the restricted rules.

The rule is not in effect before this instant. `None` means "since
forever".

Seconds until a locked-out account may try again, present only on that refusal. The number
rather than a sentence, so the console can render it in the viewer's own language.

Days left before the caller's password expires, present only inside the rotation warning
window. Advisory: a client that ignores it is never broken by one.

SliConfig.description:
What "good" means, tagged on [`SliType`] (§6b.7).

`group_by` is deliberately **not** here — it lives on [`SloDefinition`],
the single source of truth for slice identity.
**Adjacently tagged** (`{"sli_type": …, "config": {…}}`) rather than
internally tagged, because `TimeSlice` carries an `f64` threshold and this
workspace's `serde_json` has `arbitrary_precision` enabled — see
[`CountSource`] for the full explanation. `sli_type` stays a top-level key
so the storage layer can keep denormalizing it into `slos.sli_type` for
list filtering.

absent_is_bad.description:
Freshness semantics: a slice the query PROVED empty is **bad**
rather than a gap. For a pipeline-freshness SLO, absence is the
failure signal — a silent pipeline is a broken pipeline, and under
S-8's default it could never read as bad.

Only flips the meaning of a *successful* query's empty bucket; a
FAILED query still writes nothing and coverage falls, so a search
outage freezes the SLO exactly as before. That distinction is
structural — gap fill runs only after a successful query.

`#[serde(default)]` is the upgrade guarantee: every stored
time-slice SLO predates the field and keeps S-8 byte-for-byte.
Ungrouped SLOs only (validated) — gap fill cannot see a group that
is absent from the whole pass, so a grouped freshness SLO would
freeze instead of firing for precisely the failure it watches for.

comparator.description:
Orderable comparators only — a slice with no value is a *gap*, not
a failure, so `=`/`!=` have no meaning here.

allOf.description: Everything a slice's meaning depends on.

definition_generation.description:
Bumped by every computation-affecting edit, including reverts (D59).
Also the writing epoch and the CAS fence for writer commits.

groups_estimate.description:
Preflight `COUNT(DISTINCT …)` estimate; feeds the S-10 cap and the
S-14 budget.

groups_reserved.description: Budget reservation: 1 when ungrouped, else `clamp(2 × estimate, 64, hard cap)`.

target.description: Percentage in (0, 100), up to 3 decimals. Applied at READ time.

SloAlertKind.description: The two SLO-alert shapes we offer.

SloCondition.description:
The SLO alert's condition, persisted in `alerts.query_slo_condition`
(D42). `slo_id` is additionally written to the indexed `alerts.slo_id`
column, which is authoritative for reverse lookups (D60).

critical.description:
Finite and strictly positive (SA-3).

Lenient deserialization is required, not cosmetic: this struct arrives
nested inside `CreateAlertRequestBody`'s `#[serde(flatten)]`, and a
flatten buffers through `Value`, where `arbitrary_precision` represents
every number as a map (D61). A plain `f64` fails there with
`invalid type: map, expected f64`.

long_window_secs.description:
`BurnRate` only. 1h–48h, ≤ the SLO window, an exact multiple of and
≥ 2× the slice interval (SA-8).

multi_alert.description: Per-group fan-out — Feature 3's flag, same semantics (SA-13).

short_window_secs.description: `BurnRate` only. Defaults to long ÷ 12 (Google SRE workbook).

allOf.description:
Flattened, so `sli_type` and `config` sit at the SLO's top level rather
than nested under `sli_config`. `SloDefinition` is itself flattened
into [`Slo`], so this is what makes the wire shape
`{"sli_type": "count", "config": {...}, "target": ...}` — one flat
object, matching what the form actually posts.

SloDefinition.description:
The computation-affecting shape of an SLO — everything a slice's meaning
depends on.

Deliberately excludes `target`: it is applied at read time (D56), so
editing it never invalidates a slice and never triggers a rebuild.

oneOf.description:
`None` until the first pass has measured anything. Deliberately not
zeroed: "not yet measured" and "measured as zero" are different, and a
UI that conflates them shows a brand-new SLO as 0% available.

SloListItem.description: An SLO plus its current measurement, which is what a list view needs.

SloStatusView.description: What the UI and the API render for one SLO or one group.

burn_rate.description: Current burn rate — multiples of the budget-neutral rate.

coverage.description: Fraction of the window actually measured, 0..1.

error_budget_remaining.description:
**Percentage** of the error budget still unspent, not a fraction.
Negative once the budget is overspent, which is meaningful and
deliberately not clamped: "-80% remaining" is what a user needs to see
when they have burned 180% of the budget.

measuring_since.description:
The earliest instant this SLO is allowed to measure from, epoch seconds
— set only when it is LATER than the window's own start, i.e. only when
it is the reason the window is not full (S-16 PR 4).

An alert-sourced SLO cannot measure back to the start of its window: it
has no evidence before the ledger begins, and history before the source
alert's last edit was produced under a config the eligibility rules
never saw. The window is therefore genuinely partial for a while, and
the honest reading is "measuring since <date>, N of 30 days" rather than
a coverage percentage that invites the user to hunt for a gap that does
not exist.

no_data.description:
True when coverage is below the floor. Every derived figure is `None`
in that case — the SLO is frozen, not healthy and not breached.

sli.description: Percentage, 0..100. `None` when frozen or not yet measured.

stale_watermark.description:
The OTHER freeze door (§2). A source that stops evaluating leaves the
window pinned with its coverage still high, so [`Self::no_data`] — which
is the coverage floor and nothing else — cannot see that freeze at all.
Set by the read path, which knows the clock; `derive` has no opinion.

time_to_exhaust_secs.description:
Seconds until the budget is exhausted at the current burn. `None` when
the burn is at or below neutral, because nothing is being exhausted.

watermark_end.description:
How far measurement actually got, epoch seconds. Reads up to ~K
recompute slices later than the last real evaluation (§2) — close
enough for a banner, and the only timestamp there is.

SnapshotCurrent.description: The hot snapshot half: rewritten on state change (~1-2KB).

SnapshotHistory.description: The cold snapshot half: rewritten on day rollover or notice change (~30KB).

SnoozeRequest.description: Not an acknowledgement: the ladder resumes when the snooze lapses.

minutes.description: `1`–`1440`: negative silences a live page into the past, unbounded overflows the i64.

Sparkline.description:
Optional trend sparkline drawn inside the metric ("Metric Text") panel — the
value + a small line/area/bar chart of the underlying series (KPI stat card).

SplunkTokenAction.description: Requested change to a Splunk HEC token.

StatusPagePreview.description:
The admin preview response: both snapshot halves through the exact same
serializer the public plane uses, so preview cannot diverge from what
visitors will see once published.

SteerOutcome.description: The steer route's 201 body; `steer.status` may be `rejected`.

question_id.description: `callID` of the `ask_responders` call this row answers.

SteerRequestBody.description: Derive author from authentication and reject unknown body fields.

hypothesis_id.description: For `hypothesis_action`: the hypothesis id in the run's ledger.

text.description: The message; ignored for `hypothesis_action`, where the server writes the text.

can_steer.description: The run takes messages and the user may send them.

items.description: The run's rows in `created_at` order, merged with what the transcript shows.

inherited_retention_days.description: Days the stream keeps data with no value of its own, 0 for forever; set by the schema read.

is_internal.description: True for streams OpenObserve writes itself; omitted when false.

StreamInfo.description: Information about a stream where a service was discovered

dropped_dimensions.description:
Identity dimensions that could not be resolved to a queryable field on
this stream's schema and were therefore omitted from `filters`.
Consumers should warn: queries on this stream are wider than the chips imply.

filters.description:
Optional filter conditions that identify this service in the stream
Example: {"namespace": "production", "cluster": "us-east-1"}

stream_type.description:
Stream type (logs, metrics, traces, profiles)

This field explicitly identifies the stream type, enabling UIs to:
1. Query the correct API endpoint (logs/_search vs metrics/_search)
2. Display appropriate type badges/icons
3. Handle flattened stream lists without losing type information

StreamPartitionTimeLevel.description: A stream's partition level per day; a day's level never changes once the day has begun.

dynamic.description: The stream's own classifier switch; unset follows `ZO_DYNAMIC_PARTITION_STREAM_TYPES`.

num_user_streams.description: Streams holding data the user sent; `num_streams` also counts the ones O2 writes itself.

SubjectRef.description:
Points at one firing of one thing. `source_id` is the rule or check that
produced it; `firing` counts firings of that source. Together they form the
`subject_id` stored on the record.

firing.description: 1-based firing counter. The first firing of a source is `#1`.

source_id.description: The rule, check or incident this firing came from.

SubjectType.description: What kind of thing paged a human.

oneOf.description: Graded runs only.

causes.description: `multiple_root_causes` only: each root cause, in first-seen order.

oneOf.description: Why the band is what it is; graded runs only.
Completed runs only.
Live only.

needs.description: Blocked runs: the title of the first blind spot with a fix.

oneOf.description: Completed runs only.
Live only.

SummaryCause.description: One root cause of a run with several.

band.description: This cause's own band, never above the claimed one.

evidence_numbers.description: Numbers of the evidence entries that cite this hypothesis.

unverified_ids.description: Evidence ids of this hypothesis that did not verify.

lead_author.description: The email of the author of the subject hypothesis' first steering lead.

evidence_numbers.description: Numbers of the verified entries of the entry's evidence ids.

alert_if_fails.description: Alert only after this many consecutive failures (like alerts trigger_tolerance).

oneOf.description: Optional authentication config (basic auth, bearer token, etc.).

collect_rum_data.description: Collect RUM data for browser checks (session replay / performance).

config.description: Type-specific config, stored as JSONB. Shape depends on check_type.

cookies.description:
Cookies injected into the browser context before any steps run.
Orthogonal to auth — can be combined with basic/bearer auth.

cooldown_mins.description: Silence period (minutes) between repeated alert notifications.

destinations.description: Alert destination names to notify on check failure.

environments.description: Environments this check runs against, by id.

folder_id.description:
Folder this synthetic belongs to, as the public folder slug the API
accepts and returns; it is resolved to the `folders.id` KSUID on write.

frequency.description: Schedule — same modular format as reports frequency.

last_check_status.description: Denormalised status from the most recent completed check. Updated by ack handler.

last_triggered_at.description: When the scheduler last fanned out this synthetic (microseconds). UI: "LAST CHECK".

next_run_at.description: Pre-computed next fire time (microseconds). 0 = fire on first tick.

owner.description: Email of the user who created this synthetic. Set on create, never updated.

retries.description: Number of retries before marking a check failed (0 = no retry).

session_replay.description: Enable session replay capture (browser checks only).

start.description:
Unix epoch microseconds — when to first run the check ("schedule later").
When set, the scheduler uses this as the initial next_run_at instead of firing immediately.

template.description: Template override for this check's messages; null or "" uses the destination's.

tz_offset.description: UTC offset in minutes, used only when `frequency.timezone` is absent or unparseable.

variables.description: Key-value variables injected into the probe environment.

wait_before_retry_secs.description: Seconds to wait between retry attempts.

oneOf.description: Reference to a secret stored in OO secrets manager.

value.description: Cookie value — encrypted at rest with org DEK.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name (e.g. "America/New_York"). Used for cron scheduling and display.

oneOf.description: Omitted for a check that holds no subtest reference.

referenced_by.description: How many checks embed this one as a subtest.

references.description: Subtest steps this browser check holds; None for protocol checks.

steps.description: Executed (expanded) steps, browser only: what bills and draws down the pool (§5.11).

example.description: Placeholder shown in the UI when secure=true and value is empty/redacted.

secure.description:
UI display flag: true = mask value as ••••. No effect on storage — all values are
AES-encrypted at rest unconditionally.

SyntheticsAlertDecision.description:
The notification a completed run should send, resolved against the check's
`alert_if_fails` / `cooldown_mins` settings and its persisted alert state.

SyntheticsBrowserDevice.description: One engine+device combination with a pre-generated execution_id (from the scheduler).

SyntheticsCapabilitiesV2.description: Capabilities response sourced from the location registry.

SyntheticsDevice.description:
A device class with its viewport dimensions — returned by the capabilities
endpoint.

SyntheticsIngestInfo.description: Ingest destination for probe result records.

step_stream.description:
One row per (execution, step) — the step-grain stream (B10).

Sent explicitly rather than derived as `{stream}_steps` by convention.
A convention is undocumented coupling: a reader of either side cannot see
it, and renaming the results stream would silently redirect step writes.
Both sides are ours and the feature is dev/introspection-only, so there is
no version-skew argument for guessing.

Written by the BROWSER probe only. Steps are a browser concept; protocol
checks have no steps and the Go agent never writes here.

stream.description: One row per execution. Carries `last_attempt_steps` as a JSON blob.

alert.description:
Whether this completed run should notify, and with what.

The caller used to notify on every completed run that had a destination,
which ignored `alert_if_fails` and `cooldown_mins` entirely. The
decision belongs here because it needs the persisted failure streak,
which only the ack path holds.

failing_environments.description: Environments of this run that did not pass, worst first, by name.

failing_locations.description:
Locations of this run's jobs that did not pass, worst first.

Empty unless the run completed and something failed. Without it a
notification for a six-location check could only say "the check is
failing" — the reader had to open the UI to find out where.

job_count.description: Total number of jobs (locations) in this run — for notification context.

passing_locations.description:
Locations of this run's jobs that passed, alphabetical.

Carried alongside the failing set because a recovery notification has no
failing locations to name — that is what "recovered" means — so without
this the message degraded to a bare count. Both sides also make a
partial recovery expressible.

run_status.description:
Aggregate run status string when run_complete = true: "passed"|"warning"|"failed"|"error".
None while the run still has pending jobs.

status_reason.description:
Runs that had failed back to back when `alert` was resolved. 0 unless
firing — a notification that says "failing" is more useful when it also
says for how long.
Why the run was a warning, echoed from the ack so the notification can say
"the certificate is expiring" rather than a generic "degrading".

browser_devices.description:
One entry per engine+device combination — browser checks only. Empty for protocol
checks.

env_inject.description:
Decrypted credential env vars for this check, sent over TLS.
Keys: `_AUTH_USERNAME`, `_AUTH_PASSWORD` (basic) or `_AUTH_TOKEN` (bearer).
Auth is redacted from `check.auth` — probe reads credentials from here only.
Empty when the synthetic has no auth configured.

oneOf.description:
Result-stream destination + the org's `o2oi_` ingest token, looked up at
resolve time (01 §7.1) so it is never at rest in the queue. Consumed by
agent-mode probes; the Lambda path receives ingest creds in the invoke
payload instead. None when the org has no enabled ingest token.

location_label.description: Human-readable location label (falls back to the id if the row is gone).

metadata.description:
Check-level metadata from the job row — flattened into stream records by the probe.
Today carries `tags`; future fields added to `JobMetadata` flow automatically.

ssrf_policy.description:
"strict" (public pools) | "relaxed" (private locations — probing the
customer's own network is the point; loopback/metadata still blocked).

synthetic.description: The synthetic definition (terminology rule: never "check" on the wire).

valid_until.description: Drop-dead time for stale catch-up work (mirrors the job row).

SyntheticsVariableKind.description: Whether a value is ever readable again after it is written.

used_by.description: Names of those checks, so a destructive action can list them before it is confirmed.

SyntheticsVariableView.description: What every read path returns for a shared variable.

SyntheticsViewport.description: Viewport dimensions delivered to the probe so it doesn't need hardcoded device tables.

updated_by.description: User who last updated this setting

SystemSettingPayload.description: Request to create or update a setting

TakeOverRequest.description: Admin body to take over a link; a publisher other than the one the caller saw is a 409.

Team.description: A group of people who can be paged together.

channel_destinations.description:
Alert Destination names this team is talked to on — the room the record
is posted to, as opposed to the people the ladder wakes.

`None` means never set and falls back to
`EscalationPolicy::destinations`, so stored policies keep working;
`Some([])` means deliberately no channel. Precedence lives in
`config::meta::oncall::policy::team_channel`.

On the team rather than the policy because a team's room is not a
property of its ladder — you want it without editing a rung — and a
whole-row super-cluster snapshot built from `Team` would otherwise have
to carry a column it cannot see.

slack_enterprise_id.description:
Slack Enterprise Grid id of the team's room, if any; matched with `slack_workspace_id`
by the Slack app's team rule (D45).

slack_same_room_destination.description: The team's webhook destination that posts to the same Slack room.

slack_workspace_id.description: Slack team id of the team's room, set by `/o2 oncall here` (RO-1).

timezone.description:
IANA name, used to render schedules in the team's own working hours.
Stored, not interpreted — resolution is in absolute micros.

source.description: `team` or `policy`, or "pages still go to the old room" is unanswerable from the API.

TeamChannelResponse.description: A team's channel and where the answer came from.

upcoming_from.description: The forward window the shares are measured over.

TeamMember.description:
Membership — a flat list of who is on the team.

Deliberately carries no level. Which rung somebody covers is a property of
the rotation (`Schedule.rotations`): a person is on the team, and the
schedule says when they are primary, secondary, or neither. A level here
would force one row per level per person and split one fact across two
places.

TeamOverview.description: The team screen's header, in one read.

acked_under_5m_percent.description:
Pages acknowledged within five minutes, as a whole percent of the pages
that were acknowledged at all. `None` when nothing was acknowledged — a
zero would read as "we are slow" rather than "nothing happened".

alerts_assigned.description:
Alert rules whose own `oncall_team` field names this team.

"Assigned" and not "owned" on purpose. Alerts that would reach this team
through one of its ownership rules are not counted and not approximated:
an alert's identity dimensions are not known until it fires, so at rest
there is nothing to match a rule against.

covered_now.description:
A page raised right now would reach somebody.

Asks the default slot, not every slot, and so is deliberately not
`!on_call_now.is_empty()`. A team whose secondary is staffed and whose
primary is not wakes nobody when the alert fires, so reporting it as
covered would be a badge that lies and would disagree with
`/coverage-gaps` and `/config-risks`.

on_call_now.description:
Everybody on call in any slot — the wider question, kept wide on
purpose. This is who to *show*; `covered_now` is whether a page lands.

ownership_paths.description:
Identity-dimension paths this team owns.

A separate number because an ownership rule is a path, not an alert rule:
`k8s-cluster=prod` is one row here and may catch a thousand alerts or
none. Folding the two into one "owns N" would state something that is not
true of either.

TeamPageStats.description: What a team's last N days looked like, in six numbers.

acked_under_5m.description:
Acknowledged within five minutes of opening — the number a team
actually manages against.

night_pages.description:
Opened inside one of `night_windows`, which the caller computes in the
team's own zone. "2am" is a fact about a person, not about UTC.

reached_final_rung.description:
Climbed to the last rung its own priority's ladder has — which, in the
shipped default policy, is the whole team.

reached_second_rung.description: Climbed past the first rung, so the first person did not answer.

TeamReachability.description: The team-level roll-up: "5 of 6 team members".

smtp_configured.description:
Whether this deployment has an SMTP transport and a valid From address. One false here
explains every unreachable row below it, and a team screen that did not
say so would read as "our people are misconfigured".

unreachable_members.description:
The people a page would be silently dropped for, named. The sentence
the UI puts under the count.

TeamSlackTestResponse.description: RO-6: what a test post to the team's Slack channel found.

TeamSlackView.description:
What the team-channel read and write show of the team's Slack channel (RO-1, RO-2); never its
workspace id.

slack_connected.description: The org has an active Slack app installation.

slack_native.description: Pages post in the channel through a Slack app installation serving the org.

slack_same_room_destination.description: Only while it is still one of the team's webhook destinations.

slack_unavailable_reason.description: SA-8 / RO-2: why pages cannot post in Slack.

TelephonyState.description: The wire name of a [`TelephonyStatus`]'s state, serialized snake_case.

TelephonyStatus.description: The live state of the account an org would page with; never a SID or token.

TelephonyView.description: What the Telephony page shows; never a token, never the deployment's SID (U7, P6).

press4_available.description: Whether calls can offer "press 4 to acknowledge", which needs a callback URL.

applies_to.description: Kinds the template is meant for; [] is every kind. Absent on update keeps the stored list.

isPrebuilt.description:
True for system-managed prebuilt templates (those whose name starts
with `prebuilt_`). The public API refuses updates and deletes for
these, so the UI should render them as read-only.

kind.description:
Template kind: "custom" (default) or "content". Absent on write means
"unspecified" — create defaults to custom, update preserves the
stored kind (sticky-kind rule, design §6.2).

type.description:
Indicates whether the body is
http or email body

empty_variables.description: Variables the draft uses that render blank in the previewed kind's sample.

variable_groups.description: `common` and one group per kind whose producer renders templates in this release.

variables.description: Every variable a template of the requested kind can use.

TestModelMatchRequest.description: Request body for the test-model-match endpoint.

attributes.description: Optional span attributes (e.g. {"openai.response.service_tier": "flex"}) for tier rules.

match_pattern.description:
An unsaved rule pattern to preview. When set, the response lists in `captured_models`
every known model this pattern would price if it were saved in this org. The
`model_name` test is unaffected and still runs against the saved rules.

model_name.description:
The model name to test (e.g. "gpt-4o", "claude-opus-3-5"). Empty skips the single-name
test, e.g. when only previewing `match_pattern`.

rule_id.description:
Id of the rule being edited. It is left out of the preview, so its saved pattern does
not compete with the edited one.

timestamp.description:
Optional span timestamp in microseconds. When provided, only definitions
whose `valid_from` <= timestamp are considered, and tiers restricted to
recurring UTC time-of-day windows (peak / off-peak) are resolved against it.

usage.description:
Optional token counts keyed by usage type (e.g. {"input": 1000, "output": 500}).
When provided, cost is calculated using the matched pricing definition.

captured_models.description:
The known models the previewed `match_pattern` would price, the model the pattern names
first. Empty when no pattern was sent.

oneOf.description:
How the matched pattern covers the model name: `exact` when it matches the whole name,
`approximate` when the name continues before or after the match (the price may belong
to a different model). Null if nothing matched.
The matched pricing definition, or null if no definition matched.

tier.description: The name of the selected pricing tier, or null if no definition matched.

tier_index.description: Index of the selected tier in `matched.tiers`, which stays unambiguous when names repeat.

TestPageRequest.description: Priorities page differently, so the caller has to say which ladder to prove.

priority.description: Defaults to P2, the highest priority whose ladder starts with one person, not everyone.

attempts.description:
Attempts the registered retry policy took. A bench runs the same policy
a real Slot would, so this is how a reader sees a retried sample.

TestRunSampleBody.description:
One sample a test run should try: a hand-entered input or a Dataset row the
caller already resolved.

rowId.description:
A stable handle to line a result back up with its input. A Dataset row
id, or a caller-chosen label for a hand-entered sample.

ThreadQuestion.description: A question the agent asked the responders.

answered_at.description: µs: when that answer reached the session.

answered_by.description: The author of the first answer to it.

ended_at.description: `null` while this is the open step of a live run.

from_steering.description: The first step that starts after the agent read a steering message.

stage.description: `null` for tool calls made before the first `record_step`.

output.description: Only with the org setting `ai_rca_thread_tool_output`; at most 16 KB.

question_id.description: The question an answer replies to.

read_at.description: µs: when the agent read the message.

oneOf.description: Comparison operator

value.description: Threshold value (e.g., 200000 for extended context pricing)

TierRule.description: A rule on a span attribute; `keys` are tried in order and the first present one is compared.

keys.description: Attribute keys tried in order; compared ignoring case and `_`/`-`/`.` separators.

oneOf.description: Comparison operator; one this build does not know parses as `unknown` and never matches.

values.description: Accepted values for `in` / `not_in`, compared trimmed and case-insensitively.

TimeRangePolicy.description: The ranges a link offers; with more than one, viewers can switch between them.

partial.description:
True when the scan timed out while expanding this found range, so the
range is a lower bound of the real one; retry may extend it.

TimeRangeStatus.description:
Per-key lookup verdict. `NotFound` means the searched bounds were fully
scanned without a hit; `Timeout` means the scan gave up, so the key may
still exist.

ToolsetKind.description: The type of AI toolset integration.

ToolsetListResponse.description: Response body for the list endpoint.

ToolsetResponse.description:
Single toolset as returned by the API.

Always construct via [`ToolsetResponse::from_toolset`] to ensure sensitive
credential values are redacted before the response leaves the server.

data.description: Kind-specific JSON config with sensitive values redacted.

TopologyMeta.description: The v4 job's progress and unresolved counts behind a topology response.

degraded.description: Non-essential queries that failed and were read as empty.

processed_up_to.description: Seconds; max over the org's trace streams.

source.description: Always "v4"; kept so the response shape does not change.

TraceDetailsCursor.description: Keyset cursor; `start_time` is a string because 19-digit ns lose precision as JSON numbers.

oneOf.description: Send back as `after_start_time` and `after_span_id` to fetch the next page.
Legacy single-id field; always null for multi-id requests.

Transcript.description: Whether the run's chat transcript can be read.

notify_on_warning.description:
Whether a Warning-level match delivers a notification (D11).
`None` = true — warnings notify unless explicitly opted out.
Persisted in `trigger_thresholds`.

warning_threshold.description:
Warning threshold, sharing `operator` with `threshold` — one operator
for both levels, no mixed directions (T-2). `None` = single-level
alert, i.e. exactly the legacy behaviour.
Validated by `level::validate_thresholds` — "less severe" is
direction-dependent, so this is NOT simply `< threshold`.

TriggerRcaBody.description: Optional body of `POST …/rca`: guidance for the new run. Unknown fields are refused.

guidance.description: What the responder wants this analysis to look at; 1 to 2000 characters.

Unavailability.description:
One stretch during which a person is not to be given a shift.

Org-wide, not per team: being on holiday is a fact about a person, and
somebody on two teams is away from both. Per team, the window has to be
written twice, and forgetting the second is the exact failure this prevents
— a page landing on somebody who is on a beach.

Absolute micros, like an override. Recurrence is a calendar feature, and a
schedule that guesses which Fridays somebody meant guesses wrong at 3am.

end_at.description:
Exclusive, matching every other boundary here: the end instant already
belongs to the shift they are back for.

user_email.description: Whose absence. Email, because email is the login.

oneOf.description: Null when no definition matches the model today.

priced_now.description: An exact definition covers new spans; these older spans retain their recorded cost.

UnpricedModelMatch.description: The pricing definition a listed model resolves to today.

UnpricedModelRow.description: A model whose spans in the window were priced approximately or not at all.

agent_count.description: Distinct agent names behind the row, including those past the cap.

agents.description: Up to [`MAX_AGENT_NAMES`] agent names that sent the model.

cost.description: Cost recorded at ingest (0 for unpriced spans).

model.description: Null for spans that carry no model name: they have tokens but nothing to price.

model_count.description:
Distinct models ingest marked in the window, uncapped and before today's prices are
applied; spans without a model name count as one.

models.description: Models with recorded pricing gaps, including those priced since ingestion.

models_truncated.description: The server listed only the models with the most tokens; `model_count` has them all.

tokens.description: Tokens on every span ingest marked in the window.

UnverifiedCitation.description: An evidence item that matches no successful tool call.

allOf.description: Alert configuration fields (used for scheduled/realtime alerts).

oneOf.description:
Alert configuration for monitoring streams and triggering notifications.

An alert watches a stream (logs, metrics, or traces) using SQL or PromQL queries,
and sends notifications to configured destinations when trigger conditions are met.

context_attributes.description: Optional key-value attributes to include in alert notifications.

creates_incident.description:
When true, this alert routes notifications through the incident system
instead of sending direct alert notifications.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this alert monitors.
description.example: Fires when error count exceeds threshold in the specified time window

destinations.description:
List of destination names to notify when alert fires.
Destinations must be pre-configured in the system.
Accepts either `destinations` or `alert_destinations` as the JSON field name.

enabled.description: Whether the alert is active. Disabled alerts are not evaluated.

id.description: Unique identifier for the alert. Auto-generated on creation.

incident_title_template.description: Incident title template; the generated title is used when no variable resolves.

is_real_time.description:
If true, alert evaluates in real-time as data arrives.

HTTP request body for `CreateAlert` endpoint.

Creates a new alert with the specified configuration. The alert monitors
a stream (logs, metrics, or traces) and triggers notifications when conditions are met.

## Example

```json
{
    "name": "High Error Rate Alert",
    "stream_type": "logs",
    "stream_name": "default",
    "is_real_time": false,
    "query_condition": {
        "type": "sql",
        "sql": "SELECT count(*) as count FROM \"default\" WHERE level = 'error'"
    },
    "trigger_condition": {
        "period": 15,
        "operator": ">=",
        "threshold": 100,
        "frequency": 5,
        "frequency_type": "minutes",
        "silence": 60
    },
    "destinations": ["slack-alerts"],
    "enabled": true,
    "description": "Alert when error count exceeds 100 in 15 minutes"
}
```

x-o2-mcp.description: Search data with SQL, you can use `match_all('foo')` to search with full text search, also you can use `str_match(field, 'bar')` to search in a specific field; start_time, end_time can't be zero, need to be a valid micro timestamp. Note: in summary mode only took/hits/total/from/size/columns/scan_size/function_error are returned; rows are never capped, so `size` is what controls how many you get. Tip: set agent_options.output_format='csv' to receive tabular hits as a compact csv block (~40% fewer tokens than json); 'md_table' for small result sets. Tip: set agent_options.mode='partition' when querying a large time range: the server scans time partitions one by one and stops early once enough rows are collected (less data scanned), and aggregation queries build up reusable cache partition by partition. Do NOT split the time range yourself and query partitions in a loop — one call does it server-side.

For pipeline destinations, this includes external systems like OpenObserve, Splunk, Elasticsearch, etc. Use the 'module' query parameter to specify destination type: 'alert' (default) or 'pipeline'.

```json
{"name": "my_webhook", "url": "https://example.com/webhook", "method": "post", "type": "http", "template": "Default"}
```

Example Email destination:
```json
{"name": "my_email", "type": "email", "emails": ["alerts@example.com"], "template": "Default"}
```

This endpoint allows meta service accounts to obtain temporary session tokens
for accessing a target organization as a specific service account. The session
automatically expires after the specified duration.

# Security
- Only meta service accounts can call this endpoint
- The service account must exist in both _meta and target organization
- The service account must have the appropriate role in the target organization
- Maximum session duration is capped at 24 hours

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:5080/api/_meta/assume_service_account \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <meta_sa_token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "org_id": "customer1",
    "service_account": "tenant_admin_sa",
    "duration_seconds": 3600
  }'
```

The job is queued for execution and returns a job ID that can be used to monitor progress and retrieve results later.

use_index.description: Set to false to skip the inverted index for this query.

post.summary: Submit search job

delete.description: Permanently deletes a search job and its associated results from the system. This action first cancels the job if it's still running, then removes all job data including metadata and stored results. Use this to clean up completed jobs and free up storage space. This operation cannot be undone.

example.message: [Job_Id: abc123] Running Search Job deleted successfully.

get.description: Retrieves the current status and metadata for a specific search job. This includes execution state, timing information, error messages if any, and other job details. Use this to monitor job progress and determine when results are ready for retrieval or if the job encountered any issues during execution.

post.description: Cancels a running or pending search job, stopping its execution and freeing up resources. This is useful for stopping long-running queries that are no longer needed or consuming too many resources. Once cancelled, the job cannot be resumed and no results will be available.

example.message: [Job_Id: abc123] Running Search Job cancelled successfully.

post.summary: Cancel search job

get.description: Retrieves the results from a completed search job with optional pagination. The job must have finished successfully before results can be accessed. Results include the matching records, total count, execution timing, and metadata. Use pagination parameters to retrieve large result sets in manageable chunks.

post.description: Retries a previously failed or cancelled search job by resubmitting it for execution. This is useful for handling transient failures or resource constraints that may have caused the original job to fail. Only cancelled or finished (failed) jobs can be retried. The job will be re-queued with the same original parameters and query.
post.summary: Retry search job

Retrieves the roles assigned to every user in the organization in a single request, returned as a map of user email to role list. Replaces issuing one request per user. Requires enterprise features to be enabled.

delete.description: Removes a user from the organization, immediately revoking their access to all organization resources, data, and services. The user account itself remains active and can be added back to organizations later. This action is permanent and cannot be undone without re-adding the user explicitly.

put.description: Updates user account information including role assignments, password changes, or other profile details. Users can modify their own account settings, while administrators have broader permissions to update any user account. Password changes require the new password to be at least 15 characters long by default or comply to the defined password policy for security compliance. Setting remove_lockout releases an active failed-login lockout and resets the counters; it answers to the same gate as an administrative password reset, so Root or Admin on the organization, and never the locked-out user themselves.

remove_lockout.description:
Releases an active failed-login lockout and resets the counters. Nothing else ends one
early — not even a password change, since the lock records attempts rather than the
password — and it is gated like a password reset by an administrator.

get.description: Performs a basic health check to verify that the OpenObserve service is running and responding to requests. Returns a simple status indicator that can be used by load balancers, monitoring systems, and orchestration platforms to determine service availability and readiness.

post.description: Ingests Real User Monitoring (RUM) log events and client-side application logs as NDJSON, one JSON object per line, or as a single JSON array of objects (the format the native mobile SDKs send). Captures browser console logs, application errors, debug information, and custom log messages generated by client-side JavaScript. Logs are enriched with browser and session context for comprehensive client-side debugging and monitoring.

requestBody.description: Ingest data (NDJSON, one JSON object per line, or a single JSON array of objects). An array must be the whole body with no trailing lines; an empty array is accepted with no records.

example.message: Error# Failed processing: each line must be a JSON object

400.description: Bad request: a line is not valid JSON, or a line or array element is not a JSON object

post.description: Ingests Real User Monitoring (RUM) session replay data as compressed multipart form data. Captures user interactions, DOM snapshots, and browser events to enable complete session replay functionality. Data is compressed using zlib compression and includes session metadata such as timing, view information, and interaction sequences for comprehensive user experience analysis.

schema.description: Multipart form data being ingested in the form of session-replay

requestBody.description: Multipart form data containing compressed session replay segment and event metadata

Data is automatically enriched with metadata and stored for analysis and dashboard visualization.
